text:
jordan: hey team, i'm landing my first PR to web-frontend (adds a small feature + tests). two quick q's: do we branch off main or dev for tiny fixes? and is there a hard rule for PR size / diff expectations? trying to avoid churn.

devon: welcome Jordan :wave: usually for bugfixes and small features we branch from main. long-running work should use feature/<ticket>-desc branches. if it's >500 LOC or touches multiple services, split it. aim for self-contained commits.

lee: fwiw our informal rule is "can a reviewer reasonably review in 15-20m?" If yes, ship as one PR. If it requires reading several files + infra, split. Also check the CODEOWNERS; touching auth or infra will need service infra reviewers.

jordan: thanks. and commit message style? we use conventional commits? any team-specific tweaks?

amy: yep conventional-ish. we prefer: type(scope): short summary (ticket). types we use: feat, fix, refactor, chore, docs. scope is optional but helpful. Example: 

feat(web): add compact search bar (#4567)

We like a brief 1-line + optional body explaining "why" and any migration notes. PR description should include screenshots for UI changes and a short QA checklist.

devon: also add the jira/ticket reference in the body under "Relates-to:". CI tooling parses it for release notes.

jordan: good to know. question about generated files — i ran the build and a bunch of compiled assets ended up in my branch. should those be committed?

lee: generally no. generated assets (dist, build/*, proto/gen) are not committed. If they accidentally landed, you can remove them with: 
```bash
# keep your source edits, remove generated files from git history in this branch
git rm -r --cached path/to/dist || true
# add proper .gitignore entries if missing
git commit -m "chore: remove generated artifacts from branch"
```
If CI expects generated files (rare), tests will flag it.

amy: quick tip on PR reviewers: add at least one person from the CODEOWNERS and one from the product team if it's a UX change. Tag @team-web in the PR description to get eyes. Small PRs get merged faster.

ci-bot: ci-bot: build #2045 \u2022 queued

devon: for branching pattern we like feat/<ticket>-shortdesc or fix/<ticket>-shortdesc. keep the branch name readable for backporting.

jordan: got it. any lint / formatting pre-commit hooks i should run?

lee: run `yarn format` and `yarn lint` locally. We have Husky hooks but they sometimes slip. Also run `yarn test:unit` for quick confidence.

amy: PR process: request reviews, wait for at least one approval from code owners, address comments in follow-up commits (or force-push if cleaning up). Squash-and-merge is our default. If you want to keep commits, say so in the PR and ping me.

jordan: thanks all — this helps a ton. i'll clean the generated cruft and push an updated branch. pinging @lee for a quick review when ready.

ci-bot: ci-bot: build #2045 \u2022 SUCCESS \u2022 all checks passed

lee: i'll take a look in ~30m. if it's small i can approve and merge. happy to pair if you want a quick walkthrough of the test harness.

jordan: sounds great, thanks! :pray:
